structured_output.summary: No confirmed defect in the nested-package git path handling, PID retention through signalling, startup heartbeat, or aggregate candidate-SHA binding in the files I read. Two issues block release. First, the aggregate gate's 'independent' acceptance evidence is a free-form workflow_dispatch string whose only provenance check is truthiness. Second, the R worker's output-limit accounting can't trip while a segment is running. I read about 8 of 69 changed files, so this is not a full review.

findings.title: Aggregate acceptance observations are self-attested and unverifiable
findings.body: validate_aggregate accepts live_smoke, package_triage, full_gates, rendered_review, adversarial_review and requirement_mapping when each has the right candidate_sha, status=='passed' and any truthy 'provenance'. .github/workflows/a2-release.yml:5-71 takes these from a free-form workflow_dispatch string and writes it to disk as data. Anyone who can dispatch the workflow can type a passing JSON blob, and the aggregate job goes green with no live smoke, review, or requirement mapping ever run. Only the two platform artifacts are produced and re-verified in CI. The spec requires independent acceptance evidence, and this gate does not provide it.
findings.recommendation: Bind each observation to a verifiable artifact, such as a content hash of an uploaded evidence file or the run ID of a CI job that produced it, and have the verifier validate it. Reject a bare truthy provenance string. Or keep the gate explicitly pending until real evidence exists.

findings.title: R output-limit accounting is only updated at segment boundaries
findings.body: evaluate::evaluate buffers all output in memory. The payload counter is incremented and payload.json is written (via checkpoint()) only after the whole segment finishes. The guardian's 10 MiB output limit (lib/_docguardian.py:90-99) therefore sees nothing from one segment that prints in a loop. Only the 60 s chunk deadline bounds it, so R can allocate gigabytes in that window and be OOM-killed. That would end as a guardian-failure or crash, not a clean output-limit result.
findings.recommendation: Bound captured output inside the segment, using a custom output handler or text connection that updates the payload counter and aborts past the limit, or add an address-space limit on the R child. Add a test for a segment that loops on print().

findings.title: Emergency killpg on a stored child PID can hit a reused PID
findings.body: When the guardian has died, the parent sends SIGKILL with os.killpg(armed['child_pid']). The leader may already have been reaped, or reparented and reaped by init, so the PGID could by then belong to an unrelated process group. The run_id check guards only against another run's armed.json, not PID reuse. This is inferred, not demonstrated, and the window is small.
findings.recommendation: Before the emergency kill, confirm the group still has a member whose start time matches the recorded child, or document the residual risk.

next_steps: Replace the self-attested observation input with hash-bound or run-bound evidence
Enforce the output limit inside R segments, and test it
